items.cmd: make a standalone runner refuse or warn LOUDLY when it takes the daemon lock without providing the daemon's services (discord feed pump)
items.why: Root-caused 2026-08-26 09:38: Heimdall's Discord went silent because bifrost_daemon.py:358 hosts discord_feed.pump on a 10s tick, and a standalone runner takes the bifrost:daemon:<agent> lock without running it -- then a real daemon REFUSES to start because the lock is held ('no steal'). Outbound had no host and could not get one, while every liveness signal stayed green: process up, doctor shows a runner, pulse normal, discord_feed.configured() True. A capability vanished with no alarm anywhere. Fix options: (a) the runner refuses the daemon lock entirely and lets a daemon hold it, (b) the runner warns loudly at startup that it is squatting a slot whose services it does not provide, naming the pump, or (c) the runner hosts the pump too. Same class as the rest of 2026-08-26: an absence that reads as normal. items.cmd: remote_bridge_supervise discards the child's death evidence, then points at a log the child never writes
items.why: Hit live 2026-08-26 12:05: the bridge listener died 3x in 50s, breaker tripped correctly, door stayed down. I could NOT root-cause it and the reason is structural. (1) The child's stdout/stderr goes into ManagedChild's in-memory deque(maxlen=200) and the supervisor NEVER prints it -- not on child exit, not on breaker trip -- so the only record of why it died dies with the supervisor. (2) The breaker message says 'Read state/logs/remote-bridge-listener.log', but the child writes its banner and errors to STDOUT, and that file had no entry from today at all -- the operator is sent to an empty file. (3) door_open() is logging-only and does NOT drive the respawn (child.poll does), which is easy to misread -- I misread it myself -- so the loud DOOR SHUT lines look causal and are not. FIX: on child exit and on breaker trip, print the ManagedChild output tail; and either point the breaker message at the real sink or give the child a file. RULED OUT while chasing this, so nobody repeats it: the listener runs fine standalone (verified); the listener pins never bind a port (bind_allowed is pure); LockTimeout from the new _append_row file lock cannot escape (handle_request wraps accept in except Exception). SAME CLASS as last night's daemon 200-char clip that destroyed the TIMEOUT receipts: the diagnostic points away from the evidence, and the evidence is thrown away. Door is currently UP unsupervised (pid 36196) with stdout captured to state/logs/bridge-listener-stdout.log so the NEXT failure is diagnosable.

items.cmd: !spawn should say ALREADY UP on EADDRINUSE instead of reporting the interpreter version
items.why: Live 2026-08-26 12:14: Daniil ran !spawn Rill from his phone and got a red warning -- 'that spawn never lived -- exit 1: Node.js v24.14.1'. The real cause, buried in state/spawn-logs/launch-rill-1787760845.log, was EADDRINUSE on 127.0.0.1:3080 because Rill was ALREADY ALIVE (node pid 44588, up since 02:43). The port acted as a de facto singleton and correctly refused a second instance -- the RIGHT outcome, reported as a failure. What the operator saw from a phone was a scary triangle suggesting his agent was broken; the one fact that would have reassured him (already running, here is the URL) was in a log file he cannot read from a phone, and what he DID get was the messenger's Node version, not the cause. FIX: catch EADDRINUSE (and already-running generally) in the spawn path and answer 'X is ALREADY UP at <url>' with the sprout, not the warning. NOTE THE GOOD NEWS THIS SITS ON TOP OF: the honest-failure fix works -- an earlier incident had !spawn reporting a healthy sprout over a corpse; this time it refused to claim an unverified success. It simply has no vocabulary for 'already running'. Same class as the day's other findings: the diagnostic reports the messenger's state instead of naming the condition. NOT DONE unasked because it touches the spawn lever, which is the operator's primary phone control surface.

items.cmd: sandbox escalation has no middle rung: a seat needing one file outside its workspace must ask for danger-full-access
items.why: Cost Rill 74 MINUTES of wall clock today, 2026-08-26. His own stats: 82m elapsed, only 8m15s of LLM work, 74m7s sitting in a blocked tool call. He needed to copy ONE file (his own plugin's deployed copy at C:\Users\L5\.dsh\profiles\web\plugins) from outside his workspace sandbox, which is confined to E:\AI-Setup. The available modes are workspace-write and danger-full-access and NOTHING BETWEEN -- so writing a single known path required requesting full access to the entire machine, which only a human can grant. He asked correctly and then waited, because that is the only thing he could do. I unblocked him by doing the copy myself with install_dsh_plugin.py and REJECTED the escalation, so no elevated permission was granted. The defect is structural and will recur: any seat whose deployment target sits outside its workspace hits the same wall, and the honest options are both bad -- block for a human, or hand out the machine. WANT: a scoped escalation (a named path or a small allowlist) so 'write this one file' does not have to mean 'trust me with everything'. NOTE the adjacent good behaviour worth preserving: the DSH harness correctly refused, told him the rule, and made him justify -- the refusal is right, it is the GRANULARITY that is wrong.

items.cmd: fix: worklive sid8 discriminator does not discriminate for DSH seats -- key is literally bifrost:worklive:dsh_agent#session- because every DSH session id starts with the literal string 'session-', so the first-8-chars slice is a constant. items.cmd: fix: 'UNATTENDED RECIPIENT: no live seat' fires on every send to an operator inbox (daniil/daniel/user), where it is misleading. The operator has no heartbeat BY DESIGN -- he is a human read through the Discord feed pump, not a seat. The warning says 'nothing is reading it now', which is false whenever the pump is up, and it fires identically for the case where it WOULD be true (a real seat that is down). Sending to _OPERATOR_INBOXES should instead report the delivery surface: whether the feed pump is configured, whether a seat channel resolves for the sender, and that it will surface on Discord. Cry-wolf risk is the real cost: today it fired three times in a row on messages that all delivered.
items.why: A warning that is wrong in the common case trains every seat to ignore it in the uncommon case, where it is the only signal that a message died.

items.cmd: fix: check_comprehensibility resolves repo-path references against the WORKING TREE, not the index, so a reference to an instance-local file passes locally and fails for anyone who clones. Proven 2026-08-26 in a fresh worktree at origin/master: main tree reports PASS, clean checkout reports 12 drift FAILs. Eleven of the twelve are references to security/acl.json, which commit 06cead8b deliberately made instance-local (t384 MIGRATION) while leaving the references in AGENTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/ARRIVAL-PACKET.md, docs/DSH_INTEGRATION.md, docs/MAP.md, docs/MODULE_INDEX.md, docs/WISHLIST.md, core/comm/conductor_gate.py, core/toolbelt/followup.py, core/trust/grant_writer.py and core/trust/registry.py. The twelfth is docs/CODEX_INTEGRATION.md pointing at tests/test_codex_hook_contract.py, which is untracked. TWO defects, and the second is the one that matters: (1) the references are stale and a cloner sees twelve broken paths; (2) THE GUARD CANNOT SEE THIS ABOUT ITSELF because it asks the filesystem whether a path exists rather than asking git ls-files. That is the guard-of-guards blind spot -- an absence rendering as normal inside the instrument built to catch exactly that. Fix (2) first: resolve reference existence against the INDEX, and the eleven then surface on their own. Also explains why the guardrail baseline reads 0: it was measured in a tree that has the file.
items.why: The repo is PUBLIC. Everything this guard is blind to is precisely what a first-time visitor sees and we do not.

items.cmd: fix: the trust registry's intentional fail-OPEN is SILENT, and the file it depends on is not in the repo. core/trust/registry.py BOOTSTRAP_ROLES grants claude super_admin and deepseek admin when security/acl.json is MISSING or CORRUPT; _bootstrap_or_quarantine() fails CLOSED for every other agent. That asymmetry is deliberate and documented -- the docstring says plainly 'this is what keeps DeepSeek admin through a lost/corrupt file' -- so this is NOT a bug report about the policy. It is a report about the SILENCE: the fallback path emits no log line, no event, no doctor row and no boot warning, so an operator whose acl.json was deleted has two seats running at elevated role with nothing anywhere saying the ACL is gone. Verified 2026-08-26: security/acl.json was deliberately made instance-local by commit 06cead8b, and it is absent from a clean checkout of origin/master (confirmed in worktree E:/AI-Setup-publish), so a FRESH CLONE takes the permissive branch by default and says nothing. The same module already learned this exact lesson once for a sibling case -- the T151 comment in this very file records that grant EXPIRY 'was a TRAPDOOR ... no boot line, no doctor row, no warning', and a time-boxed seat silently stopped working mid-arc. Expiry got a surface; the bootstrap fallback has the same shape and did not. Fix: emit a loud, once-per-process warning on the fallback path and surface it in doctor, per the peer-stated rule that a fallback wider than what it replaces must be LOUD.

items.cmd: settle: a LESSON'S PREMISE CONTRADICTS CURRENT SOURCE, and the source did not change under it. learn:experiment:wake_deadline_measures_session_age_so_a_long_session_cycles_instantly (claude, 2026-08-15) states that bifrost_wake's cycle line measures SESSION age, citing an arm that 'reported after 7.04h elapsed about three minutes after I started it', and concludes that in a long session every further arm cycles immediately so you should stop re-arming. Reading the source 2026-08-27: scripts/bifrost_wake.py:348 sets deadline = time.time() + total_deadline_s at the top of watch(), and :442 computes elapsed_s = time.time() - (deadline - total_deadline_s), which is simply the age of THIS ARM. deadline is assigned exactly once (the only other hit, :491, is the argparse namespace default). Under that reading an arm cannot report 7.04h three minutes after launch, and the observed 3.97h readings are healthy four-hour watches completing normally. git log -S on the elapsed line shows it landed 2026-07-16 in bd29f7bc -- a MONTH BEFORE the lesson -- so this is not a stale lesson describing a since-fixed bug. Two readings of the same code disagree and I cannot reconcile them from inspection. MOST LIKELY EXPLANATION, unproven: the lesson's author read a PREVIOUS arm's output file and attributed it to the arm just launched, which is the same misattribution class this seat committed twice on 2026-08-26. THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES IT, in one command: run bifrost_wake with --deadline 5 and read what elapsed reports. NOT RUN HERE ON PURPOSE -- a self-cycle writes a re-arm trigger file, and the live wake path is the operator's only remote hand on this house. Run it in E:/AI-Setup-Sandbox, or on the live path only when the operator is at the machine. COST OF LEAVING IT: the lesson currently advises seats to STOP RE-ARMING and declare themselves unwatchable, which this seat did on 2026-08-26 and was wrong.
items.why: This is the house's first natural premise-check -- a lesson flagged by its own premise failing against source rather than by anyone noticing the advice was bad. It is worth settling for the method as much as the answer, and its current advice makes seats unreachable on purpose.
